newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev eases to adjust to 1,000-per-mark peg. [CORRECTED 17:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev eases to adjust to 1,000-per-mark peg. [CORRECTED 17:15 GMT]

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 1,648-1,652 per dollar, down from 1,625-1,640 at midday and 1,630-1,655 at the opening to adjust to the upcoming 1,000 levs-per-mark currency board peg, traders said.
"Foreign curency supply fell in the afternoon and traders were aiming at higher ask prices in line with the pegging rate," a commercial bank dealer said.

The mark traded at 954-960 levs, tracking the dollar/mark cross on international markets. The dollar has around 45 percent share in local market daily turnover while trade in marks accounts for between one and 10 percent of turnover.

Parliament decided on Wednesday (corrects from Tuesday) to peg the lev at 1,000 to the mark as an anchor in a currency board arrangement and has yet to decide whether the peg will become effective immediately or from July 1, when the currency board is to be launched.
Foreign currency demand today came mainly from final clients bidding for cheaper marks ahead of the peg.

"No one is willing to buy marks at 1,000 levs now because of potential losses from the large interest rate spread if the peg goes in force on July 1. But we expect the lev to ease in the days ahead until the peg becomes effective," another dealer said.
The Bulgarian National Bank main interest rate is now set at 48.72 percent annually. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
